ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=3$, $BC=3\sqrt{3}$, and $\angle CBD=30^\circ$. Point $M$ is a point on the ray $BD$ (not coinciding with points $B$, $D$). Line $AM$ is drawn, and through point $M$, $MN \perp AM$ intersects line $BC$ at point $N$. If $\triangle BMN$ is an isosceles triangle, what is the length of $BN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect AN,\\
since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle, it follows that $\angle ABN=90^\circ$,\\
since $MN\perp AM$, it follows that $\angle AMN=90^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle BNM+\angle BAM=180^\circ$,\\
since $\angle BAM<90^\circ$, it follows that $\angle BNM>90^\circ$,\\
since $\triangle BMN$ is an isosceles triangle, there only exists the case where $BN=MN$,\\
in $Rt\triangle ABN$ and $Rt\triangle AMN$, $\left\{\begin{array}{l}AN=AN\\ BN=MN\end{array}\right.$,\\
hence $Rt\triangle ABN\cong Rt\triangle AMN\left(HL\right)$,\\
thus $AB=AM$,\\
since $\angle ABN=90^\circ$, $\angle CBD=30^\circ$, hence $\angle ABM=60^\circ$,\\
thus $\triangle ABM$ is an equilateral triangle, hence $\angle BAM=60^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle BAN=\angle MAN=\frac{1}{2}\angle BAM=30^\circ$, hence $AN=2BN$,\\
since $AB^2+BN^2=AN^2$, and $AB=3$,\\
hence $3^2+BN^2=(2BN)^2$, hence $BN=\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$.

method.method_draft: Synthetic congruence route. From the diagram, use that A is above B, BC is horizontal, M lies on diagonal BD inside the rectangle, N lies on BC, and MN is drawn perpendicular to AM. Connect AN. Since ABCD is a rectangle, AB ⟂ BN, so triangle ABN is right; also MN ⟂ AM, so triangle AMN is right. Angle chasing gives ∠BNM + ∠BAM = 180°, and because M is inside the rectangle on BD, ∠BAM < 90°, hence ∠BNM > 90°. In an isosceles triangle BMN with the obtuse angle at N, the only possible equal sides are BN = MN. Then right triangles ABN and AMN share hypotenuse AN and have one equal leg BN = MN, so by HL they are congruent, implying AB = AM and AN bisects ∠BAM. Since BD makes 30° with BC and AB ⟂ BC, ∠ABM = 60°. With AB = AM, triangle ABM has base angle at B equal to 60°, so it is equilateral and ∠BAM = 60°. Therefore ∠BAN = 30°. In right triangle ABN, AB = 3 and tan 30° = BN/AB, giving BN = 3/√3 = √3.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=3$, $BC=3\sqrt{3}$, and $\angle CBD=30^\circ$. Point $M$ is a point on the ray $BD$ (not coinciding with points $B$, $D$). Line $AM$ is drawn, and through point $M$, $MN \perp AM$ intersects line $BC$ at point $N$. If $\triangle BMN$ is an isosceles triangle, what is the length of $BN$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect AN,\\
since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle, it follows that $\angle ABN=90^\circ$,\\
since $MN\perp AM$, it follows that $\angle AMN=90^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle BNM+\angle BAM=180^\circ$,\\
since $\angle BAM<90^\circ$, it follows that $\angle BNM>90^\circ$,\\
since $\triangle BMN$ is an isosceles triangle, there only exists the case where $BN=MN$,\\
in $Rt\triangle ABN$ and $Rt\triangle AMN$, $\left\{\begin{array}{l}AN=AN\\ BN=MN\end{array}\right.$,\\
hence $Rt\triangle ABN\cong Rt\triangle AMN\left(HL\right)$,\\
thus $AB=AM$,\\
since $\angle ABN=90^\circ$, $\angle CBD=30^\circ$, hence $\angle ABM=60^\circ$,\\
thus $\triangle ABM$ is an equilateral triangle, hence $\angle BAM=60^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle BAN=\angle MAN=\frac{1}{2}\angle BAM=30^\circ$, hence $AN=2BN$,\\
since $AB^2+BN^2=AN^2$, and $AB=3$,\\
hence $3^2+BN^2=(2BN)^2$, hence $BN=\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$

Segment AM has been drawn; from M draw the oblique line MN to point N on the bottom side BC, the figure shows N between B and C, and the problem statement gives MN⊥AM. Then reason: Connect AN. Because ABCD is a rectangle, AB⊥BC, and N is on BC, so AB⊥BN, ∠ABN=90°, and △ABN is a right triangle. Also because MN⊥AM, ∠AMN=90°, and △AMN is a right triangle. From the figure, M is inside the rectangle and on BD, ∠BAM<90°, so ∠BNM>90°. △BMN is an isosceles triangle, and ∠BNM is an obtuse angle; an obtuse angle cannot be a base angle, therefore the two equal sides of the isosceles triangle can only be BN and MN, namely BN=MN. Thus Rt△ABN and Rt△AMN have common hypotenuse AN, and one right side BN=MN, so by HL congruence, obtain AB=AM, and AN bisects ∠BAM. Also ∠CBD=30°, AB⊥BC, so ∠ABM=90°−30°=60°.
